title: RAW_UNREVIEWED: upper-link endpoint scope across three admitted text sites
summary: GDT859 fixes an upper contact over a definite group seam at f56r.1; GDT861 records an extended link at f100r.12 and a no-link at f114r.1; GDT866 finds no complete intervening group under a separate f95v2 span. Test the narrower source mechanism that the links join selected adjacent tall-stroke assemblies regardless of transcribed group boundaries, rather than mark an entity code or enclose a whole intervening written group. Compare only those already admitted native sites, with endpoints and physical gaps fixed before scoring. This would identify graphic scope, not word meaning or a general cipher rule.

design.mechanism: An upper-link stroke targets neighboring tall assemblies at the graphic level and can cross a transcription separator without spanning an independent intervening group.
design.unit: Fixed f56r.1, f100r.12, f114r.1 and f95v2 native localities already admitted under GDT859/861/866.
design.contrast: Adjacent tall-assembly linkage versus a transcribed word-level scope mark or universal entity-code mark.
design.prediction: Positive links terminate at adjacent tall assemblies when judged by native gaps; one clearly bounded complete intervening group under a link defeats the narrow graphic-scope model. The f114r no-link rules out a universal codepoint correspondence. If endpoint alignment remains uncertain, return MISSING_SOURCE_ALIGNMENT.
design.scope: Raw exploratory comparison of retained native observations; no new image admission, entity reinterpretation, semantic export or automatic expansion.
